title: DECISION: deviceDeliveredAt suppressed on receipt-sharing opt-out, same as readAt
description:
Choice: When the effective receiptSharing preference is false, the server MUST NOT record deviceDeliveredAt — it is explicitly classified alongside readAt as a privacy-sensitive user-activity timestamp, not alongside deliveredAt (which is permitted even when sharing is off).

Why good: deviceDeliveredAt reveals that the user's device was active and processed the notification — information that is behaviorally equivalent in sensitivity to readAt. Treating it like deliveredAt (a server-to-server relay event) would leak user-activity data despite the opt-out.

Alternatives avoided: Allowing deviceDeliveredAt when receiptSharing is false (privacy leak); suppressing deliveredAt as well (overreach — server delivery confirmation is not user-activity data).
